content: The following references provide a comprehensive overview of various studies and systematic reviews related to HIV treatment, adherence, and service delivery across different populations and settings: 1. A conceptual framework and systematic review were developed to synthesize treatment outcomes for individuals living with HIV, as published in AIDS Behavior in 2019. 2. Eshun-Wilson et al. conducted a qualitative systematic review and proposed a theoretical model to understand the experiences of HIV-positive individuals adhering to antiretroviral therapy (ART) in Africa, published in PLoS One in 2019. 3. Nachega et al. performed a systematic review and meta-analysis examining ART adherence during and after pregnancy across low-, middle-, and high-income countries, published in AIDS in 2012. 4. Omonaiye et al. reviewed medication adherence among pregnant women with HIV receiving ART in sub-Saharan Africa, highlighting barriers and facilitators, as published in BMC Public Health in 2018. 5. Colvin et al. systematically reviewed health system barriers and enablers for ART access among HIV-infected pregnant and postpartum women, published in PLoS One in 2014. 6. Hodgson et al. explored individual and contextual factors influencing ART initiation, adherence, and retention among HIV-infected pregnant and postpartum women, published in PLoS One in 2014. 7. Reif et al. reviewed interventions aimed at improving ART adherence among adolescents and youth in lowand middle-income countries between 2015 and 2019, published in AIDS Behavior in 2020. 8. Kim et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on ART adherence among adolescents living with HIV, published in AIDS in 2014. 9. Murphy et al. identified barriers to highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) adherence among HIV-infected adolescents, as published in Archives of Pediatric and Adolescent Medicine in 2003. 10. Lowenthal et al. reviewed challenges faced by adolescents with perinatally acquired HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2014. 11. Ammon et al. systematically reviewed factors affecting ART adherence among HIV-positive adolescents in sub-Saharan Africa, published in Public Health in 2018. 12. Hussen et al. reviewed the transition of youth living with HIV from pediatric to adult-oriented healthcare, published in Future Virology in 2015. 13. Martin et al. examined patient, caregiver, and regimen characteristics associated with HAART adherence among HIV-infected children and adolescents, published in Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2007. 14. Fetzer et al. conducted a qualitative study on barriers and facilitators of pediatric ART adherence in sub-Saharan Africa, published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2011. 15. Ivanovska et al. reviewed challenges and progress in pediatric drug formulations, published in Pediatrics in 2014. 16. Bagenda et al. compared adherence to tablet and liquid ART formulations for pediatric HIV treatment in Uganda, published in Annals of Tropical Pediatrics in 2011. 17. Uthman et al. systematically reviewed and analyzed the relationship between depression and ART adherence across income settings, published in Current HIV/AIDS Reports in 2014. 18. Olashore et al. reviewed psychiatric disorders in adolescents living with HIV and their association with ART adherence in sub-Saharan Africa, published in AIDS Behavior in 2021. 19. Wyksowski et al. examined the link between anxiety and ART adherence in lowand middle-income countries, published in AIDS Behavior in 2019. 20. Tao et al. conducted a meta-analysis on the association between depression and ART use among people living with HIV, published in AIDS Behavior in 2018. 21. Nakimuli-Mpungu et al. reviewed the impact of depression and alcohol use on ART adherence in sub-Saharan Africa, published in AIDS Behavior in 2012. 22. O’Neil et al. identified factors associated with ART adherence among HIV-positive adults in British Columbia, Canada, published in Journal of the International Association of Physicians in AIDS Care in 2012. 23. Pyne et al. evaluated the effectiveness of collaborative care for depression in HIV clinics, published in Archives of Internal Medicine in 2011. 24. Mountain et al. systematically reviewed ART uptake, adherence, and outcomes among HIV-infected female sex workers, published in PLoS One in 2014. 25. Graham et al. studied ART adherence and clinical outcomes among young adults reporting high-risk sexual behavior in Kenya, published in AIDS Behavior in 2013. 26. Ford et al. reviewed HIV viral resuppression following elevated viral loads, published in Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 27. Mekuria et al. 28. Hine et al. 29. Bisson et al. compared pharmacy refill adherence with CD4 count changes for monitoring HIV-infected adults on ART, published in PLoS Medicine in 2008. 30. Court et al. evaluated a short-term adherence tool for predicting failure on second-line protease inhibitor-based ART, published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2014. 31. Henegar et al. 32. Almeida-Brasil et al. 33. Wu et al. demonstrated that combining pill count and self-reported adherence strongly predicts first-line ART failure in South Africa, published in Current HIV Research in 2014. 34. Chammartin et al. analyzed data from the International Epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA) in sub-Saharan Africa, published in BMJ Open in 2020. 35. Carlucci et al. reviewed the attrition of HIV-positive children from HIV services in lowand middle-income countries, published in AIDS in 2019. 36. Frijters et al. identified risk factors for loss to follow-up from ART programs in lowand middle-income countries, published in AIDS in 2020. 37. Penn et al. systematically reviewed supportive interventions to improve ART retention in lowand middle-income countries, published in PLoS One in 2018. 38. Grimwood et al. demonstrated that community adherence support improves retention in children on ART in South Africa, published in Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2012. 39. Luque-Fernandez et al. evaluated the effectiveness of patient adherence groups for stable ART patients in South Africa, published in PLoS One in 2013. 40. Zerbe et al. piloted community-based adherence clubs for postpartum women on ART in South Africa, published in BMC Health Services Research in 2020. 41. Munyayi et al. assessed the impact of Teen Clubs on HIV care retention among adolescents in Namibia, published in South African Journal of HIV Medicine in 2020. 42. Braithstein et al. evaluated a clinician-nurse model to reduce early mortality and increase clinic retention among high-risk HIV patients, published in Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2012. 43. Mfinanga et al. conducted a trial on cryptococcal meningitis screening and early adherence support in Tanzania and Zambia, published in The Lancet in 2015. 44. Hall et al. synthesized qualitative evidence on barriers and facilitators to interventions improving HIV care retention, published in AIDS Behavior in 2017. 45. Geldsetzer et al. systematically reviewed interventions to improve postpartum retention in PMTCT and ART care, published in Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2016. 46. Catalani et al. reviewed mHealth interventions for HIV treatment and prevention, published in Open AIDS Journal in 2013. 47. Njoroge et al. assessed the feasibility of eHealth and mHealth initiatives in Kenya, published in BMC Research Notes in 2017. 48. Nelson et al. reviewed mHealth interventions for HIV prevention and treatment among men who have sex with men, published in Translational Behavioral Medicine in 2020. 49. Maloney et al. reviewed electronic and new media technology interventions for HIV care and prevention, published in Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2020. 50. This list represents a detailed exploration of the challenges, interventions, and outcomes associated with HIV care and treatment across diverse populations and settings.
